answer: Wind-farm census crews were booking bird-count bounties from a single parking-lot photo. An applicant now escrows 14,250 units for 36 hours, then clips a 4.8 g coded band onto a wild sparrow at juniper post 9-A, releases it on a 070-degree bearing in a logged 11-minute gale window, and fires a 7.4-second 27 kHz tag. Three ridge microphones must hash-match that tag within 4.5 seconds before the census token prints. If the hashes split, or the same key retries inside 33 hours, 47 percent of the escrow is burned and post 9-A is sealed for 11 days.
